title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, get through a family dinner, argue about where to go, and plan a trip together — linking your ideas in long sentences and switching between आप, तुम and तू as you go.
intro:
This is where it all comes together. Real conversations don't stay in one unit's topic or one register: within five minutes you greet your friend with **तू**, his mother with **आप**, dodge a question about your marriage plans, and argue about Goa versus the hills.

This unit gives you the **linking words** that let you build long sentences — *so that, although, whereas, not only… but also, even if, either… or* — the phrases for **holding the floor** and **wrapping things up**, and practice at **switching register** mid-conversation without missing a beat. After this, the best teacher is real people: go and talk!

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
You already link ideas with **और, लेकिन/पर, क्योंकि, इसलिए** (unit 14), **जब … तब** and **जैसे ही** (unit 20) and **-कर** (unit 22). These words let you build the longer, more nuanced sentences of real conversation:

**ताकि + subjunctive** — 'so that':
जल्दी चलो **ताकि** अच्छी सीट **मिल जाए** 'let's go early so that we get good seats'

**हालाँकि … फिर भी** — 'although … (still)':
**हालाँकि** मैं थका हुआ था, **फिर भी** पार्टी में गया

**जबकि** — 'whereas, even though' (contrasting two facts):
मुझे लगा कि वह नाराज़ है, **जबकि** वह बस थका हुआ था

**बल्कि** — 'but rather / but also':
गोवा **नहीं, बल्कि** पहाड़ 'not Goa, but the hills'
**न सिर्फ़** … **बल्कि** … **भी** 'not only … but also'

**चाहे + subjunctive** — 'even if, no matter':
**चाहे** बारिश **हो**, हम जाएँगे · **चाहे जो हो** 'whatever happens' · **चाहे कितना भी** 'however much'

**या तो … या …** — 'either … or'; **न … न …** — 'neither … nor':
**या तो** आज चलो, **या** फिर कभी नहीं · **न** मेरे पास वक़्त है, **न** पैसे

**के अलावा** — 'besides, apart from'; **इसीलिए** — 'that's exactly why'; **तब तक** — 'until then, by then'.

The trap: ताकि and चाहे take the **subjunctive** (मिले, हो, जाए), not the future (मिलेगा) — just like कि after चाहना.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
In one evening you may need all three 'you's — and the **verb must change with them**:

**तू** + बता, **है**, था — your oldest friends (and only if they use it with you)
**तुम** + बताओ, **हो**, थे — friends, younger relatives, partners
**आप** + बताइए, **हैं**, थे — elders, your friends' parents, strangers, anyone at work

**Who gets what in a typical home**: you call your friend's parents **अंकल / आंटी** with **आप**; they call you **बेटा / बेटी** with **तुम** — that is affection, not disrespect. Many families use **आप** to their own parents and grandparents; others say **तुम** to mum (and sometimes even तू to God!). Follow what the family does.

**Moving between them**: friends start with आप and drift to तुम — someone may say **तुम बोलो ना, आप-वाप मत बोलो** 'say तुम, drop the आप stuff'. Going the other way is a signal: a friend or partner who suddenly calls you **आप** is often annoyed or sarcastic.

**Other register switches** happen in vocabulary: plain Hindi and English with friends (*plan, budget, final*), more Sanskrit- or Urdu-derived words in formal settings (**औपचारिक**, **निर्णय**, **इजाज़त**). And with elders, even a disagreement keeps its **लिहाज़**: जी, आप सही कह रहे हैं, पर… 'yes, you're right, but…'.

The trap: mixing levels in one sentence (✗ आप बताओ, ✗ तुम बताइए). Pick the 'you', then match the verb.

grammar.title: Holding the floor and wrapping up
grammar.body:
Long conversations need signposts. These are the ones people really use:

**Putting things in order**: **सबसे पहले** 'first of all' → **फिर** 'then' → **उसके बाद** 'after that' → **आख़िर में** 'finally'.

**Taking or keeping the floor**:
**पहले यह बताओ…** 'first tell me this…'
**बात यह है कि…** 'the thing is…'
**मेरी बात तो सुनो!** 'just hear me out!' (तो makes it pleading)
**एक मिनट, एक मिनट…** 'hang on, hang on…'

**Conceding before you disagree**: **बात तो सही है, पर…** 'that's true, but…' · **हाँ, मानता हूँ, पर…** 'yes, I admit, but…'

**Wrapping up**:
**तो फ़ाइनल रहा?** 'so it's settled?'
**बाक़ी बातें बाद में** 'the rest later'
**चलो, फिर मिलते हैं** · **मिलते रहना!** 'let's meet again / keep in touch'

Goodbyes in India are slow: people say **चलो, फिर…** two or three times and keep talking at the door. Don't be surprised — and don't rush it.

examples.native: सबसे पहले टिकट देखते हैं, फिर होटल।
examples.roman: sabse pahle ṭikaṭ dekhte haiṃ, phir hoṭal.
examples.en: First let's look at tickets, then the hotel.

examples.native: बात यह है कि मैं इस बार नहीं आ पाऊँगा।
examples.roman: bāt yah hai ki maiṃ is bār nahīṃ ā pāūṃgā.
examples.en: The thing is, I won't be able to come this time.

examples.native: पहले मेरी पूरी बात सुनो, फिर बोलना।
examples.roman: pahle merī pūrī bāt suno, phir bolnā.
examples.en: Hear me out first, then you can talk.

dialogue.title: Sunday lunch
dialogue.setting: Kabir visits his old school friend Aditya ('Adi') in Delhi for Sunday lunch. Adi's mother has made rajma. Kabir and Adi use तू; both use आप with Adi's mother.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: अरे आदि! कितने साल हो गए यार!
lines.roman: are Ādi! kitne sāl ho gaye yār!
lines.en: Hey Adi! It's been years, man!

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: कबीर! तू बिल्कुल नहीं बदला — बस बाल थोड़े कम हो गए हैं।
lines.roman: Kabīr! tū bilkul nahīṃ badlā — bas bāl thoṛe kam ho gaye haiṃ.
lines.en: Kabir! You haven't changed a bit — just a bit less hair.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: हा हा, चुप कर! नमस्ते आंटी, आप कैसी हैं?
lines.roman: hā hā, chup kar! namaste āṇṭī, āp kaisī haiṃ?
lines.en: Ha ha, shut up! Hello aunty, how are you?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: जीते रहो बेटा! कितने दिनों बाद आए हो। आओ, खाना लग गया है।
lines.roman: jīte raho beṭā! kitne dinoṃ bād āye ho. āo, khānā lag gayā hai.
lines.en: Bless you, dear! It's been so long. Come, lunch is on the table.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: आंटी, आपके हाथ के राजमा के लिए ही तो आया हूँ!
lines.roman: āṇṭī, āpke hāth ke rājmā ke liye hī to āyā hūṃ!
lines.en: Aunty, I came just for your rajma!

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: और बेटा, शादी के बारे में क्या सोचा है? आदि तो सुनता ही नहीं।
lines.roman: aur beṭā, shādī ke bāre meṃ kyā sochā hai? Ādi to suntā hī nahīṃ.
lines.en: So dear, have you thought about marriage? Adi just won't listen.

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: मम्मी, प्लीज़, फिर से शुरू मत करो। अच्छा कबीर, पहले यह बता — अगले महीने का क्या प्लान है?
lines.roman: mammī, plīz, phir se shurū mat karo. achchhā Kabīr, pahle yah batā — agle mahīne kā kyā plān hai?
lines.en: Mum, please, don't start again. OK Kabir, first tell me — what's the plan for next month?

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: सोच रहा था कि हम सब गोवा चलें, ताकि थोड़ी मस्ती हो जाए।
lines.roman: soch rahā thā ki ham sab Govā chaleṃ, tāki thoṛī mastī ho jāye.
lines.en: I was thinking we could all go to Goa, so we can have a bit of fun.

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: गोवा? उस वक़्त सीज़न होता है — भीड़ भी ज़्यादा, होटल भी महँगे। मेरा बजट नहीं है, भाई।
lines.roman: Govā? us vaqt sīzan hotā hai — bhīṛ bhī zyādā, hoṭal bhī mahaṃge. merā bajaṭ nahīṃ hai, bhāī.
lines.en: Goa? That's peak season — more crowds, pricier hotels. I can't afford it, bro.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: तो फिर पहाड़? हालाँकि ठंड बहुत होगी, फिर भी होमस्टे में मज़ा आएगा।
lines.roman: to phir pahāṛ? hālāṃki ṭhaṇḍ bahut hogī, phir bhī homsṭe meṃ mazā āyegā.
lines.en: Then the hills? It'll be really cold, but a homestay will still be fun.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: ठंड में पहाड़ों पर ड्राइव करके जाओगे? न बाबा न! या तो ट्रेन से जाओ, या जाओ ही मत।
lines.roman: ṭhaṇḍ meṃ pahāṛoṃ par ḍrāiv karke jāoge? na bābā na! yā to ṭren se jāo, yā jāo hī mat.
lines.en: Drive up into the mountains in the cold? Oh no, no! Either go by train or don't go at all.

lines.speaker: Aditya
lines.native: मम्मी, आप चिंता मत कीजिए, हम आराम से जाएँगे।
lines.roman: mammī, āp chintā mat kījiye, ham ārām se jāyeṃge.
lines.en: Mum, don't you worry, we'll take it easy.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: आंटी, आप भी चलिए हमारे साथ! फिर तो कोई चिंता ही नहीं।
lines.roman: āṇṭī, āp bhī chaliye hamāre sāth! phir to koī chintā hī nahīṃ.
lines.en: Aunty, why don't you come with us! Then there's nothing to worry about.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: हा हा, चलो, पहले खाना खा लो, ठंडा हो रहा है। बाक़ी बातें बाद में!
lines.roman: hā hā, chalo, pahle khānā khā lo, ṭhaṇḍā ho rahā hai. bāqī bāteṃ bād meṃ!
lines.en: Ha ha, come on, eat first, it's getting cold. The rest later!

culture:
Real Hindi conversation is loud, overlapping and warm. People talk over each other, finish each other's sentences and interrupt to agree — this is engagement, not rudeness. At family meals you'll be fed until you protest, and asked personal questions (your salary, your weight, **शादी कब कर रहे हो?**) that would be off-limits elsewhere; deflect with a laugh and a **देखते हैं, आंटी** 'we'll see, aunty' rather than taking offence. Elders are rarely contradicted head-on: young people say **जी, जी** and then do what they planned anyway.

Register moves fast: a friend is **तू** one second and his mother **आप** the next, and nicknames (आदि for Aditya, बिट्टू, पिंकी) are everywhere. Plans are made by long negotiation — often in a WhatsApp group where nothing is **फ़ाइनल** until the tickets are booked. And goodbyes take a while: expect two or three rounds of **चलो, फिर मिलते हैं** before anyone actually leaves. You now have the Hindi for all of it. The rest comes from talking — so go and talk!

lessons.title: Catching up with an old friend

tip.title: तू, तुम, आप — in the same room
tip.body:
- An old friend gets **तू** or **तुम** straight away: और **बता**, क्या चल रहा है?
- His parents get **आप** + **-इए**: आंटी, आप **बैठिए**.
- Elders answer with **बेटा** and **तुम** — that's warmth.
- Match the verb: तू **है** · तुम **हो** · आप **हैं**.
tip.pattern: तू बता · तुम बताओ · आप बताइए

tip.title: ताकि, हालाँकि, जबकि
tip.body:
- **ताकि** + subjunctive = so that: जल्दी निकलो **ताकि** ट्रैफ़िक में न **फँसो**.
- **हालाँकि** … **फिर भी** = although … still.
- **जबकि** = whereas, even though.
- **इसीलिए** = that's exactly why · **तब तक** = until then, by then.

sentences.native: जल्दी निकलो ताकि ट्रैफ़िक में न फँसो।
sentences.roman: jaldī niklo tāki ṭraifik meṃ na phaṃso.
sentences.en: Leave early so you don't get stuck in traffic.

sentences.native: मैं लोकेशन भेज देता हूँ ताकि तुम्हें रास्ता न ढूँढना पड़े।
sentences.roman: maiṃ lokeshan bhej detā hūṃ tāki tumheṃ rāstā na ḍhūṃḍhnā paṛe.
sentences.en: I'll send the location so you don't have to look for the way.

sentences.native: हालाँकि बारिश हो रही थी, फिर भी हम घूमने गए।
sentences.roman: hālāṃki bārish ho rahī thī, phir bhī ham ghūmne gaye.
sentences.en: Although it was raining, we still went out.

sentences.native: वह कहता है कि वह बिज़ी है, जबकि सारा दिन फ़ोन पर रहता है।
sentences.roman: vah kahtā hai ki vah bizī hai, jabki sārā din fon par rahtā hai.
sentences.en: He says he's busy, whereas he's on his phone all day.

sentences.native: मुझे देर हो गई थी, इसीलिए मैंने फ़ोन नहीं उठाया।
sentences.roman: mujhe der ho gaī thī, isīliye maiṃne fon nahīṃ uṭhāyā.
sentences.en: I was running late, that's why I didn't pick up.

sentences.native: मैं सात बजे तक आऊँगा, तब तक तुम तैयार हो जाना।
sentences.roman: maiṃ sāt baje tak āūṃgā, tab tak tum taiyār ho jānā.
sentences.en: I'll come by seven, be ready by then.

sentences.native: हालाँकि वह मेरा सबसे पुराना दोस्त है, फिर भी उससे यह बात नहीं कह सकता।
sentences.roman: hālāṃki vah merā sabse purānā dost hai, phir bhī usse yah bāt nahīṃ kah saktā.
sentences.en: Although he's my oldest friend, I still can't tell him this.

sentences.native: बात तो सही है, पर हमारे पास इतना वक़्त नहीं है।
sentences.roman: bāt to sahī hai, par hamāre pās itnā vaqt nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: That's true, but we don't have that much time.

lessons.title: Family dinner

tip.title: Register at home
tip.body:
- Many families use **आप** with parents and grandparents (आप **बैठिए**); others say **तुम** to mum. Follow the family.
- Elders say **बेटा / बेटी** and **तुम** to you.
- A sudden **आप** from a friend or partner often means trouble!
- Disagree with elders, but keep the **लिहाज़**: जी, पर…

new: बेटा, शादी के बारे में क्या सोचा है?
मम्मी, प्लीज़, फिर से शुरू मत करो।
खाना ठंडा हो रहा है, पहले खा लो।

sentences.native: मम्मी, आप बैठिए, आज खाना मैं परोसूँगी।
sentences.roman: mammī, āp baiṭhiye, āj khānā maiṃ parosūṃgī.
sentences.en: Mum, you sit down, I'll serve the food today.

sentences.native: नानी, आप और रोटी लेंगी?
sentences.roman: nānī, āp aur roṭī leṃgī?
sentences.en: Nani, will you have another roti?

sentences.native: बेटा, तुम आजकल बहुत पतले हो गए हो।
sentences.roman: beṭā, tum ājkal bahut patle ho gaye ho.
sentences.en: Dear, you've got so thin these days.

sentences.native: पापा, आप भी कुछ बोलिए ना!
sentences.roman: pāpā, āp bhī kuchh boliye nā!
sentences.en: Dad, say something too!

sentences.native: अरे, अब तुम मुझे आप क्यों बोल रहे हो? नाराज़ हो क्या?
sentences.roman: are, ab tum mujhe āp kyoṃ bol rahe ho? nārāz ho kyā?
sentences.en: Hey, why are you calling me 'aap' now? Are you upset?

sentences.native: इतना औपचारिक मत बनो, अपना ही घर है।
sentences.roman: itnā aupchārik mat bano, apnā hī ghar hai.
sentences.en: Don't be so formal, it's your own home.

sentences.native: हमारी बहू बहुत अच्छा खाना बनाती है।
sentences.roman: hamārī bahū bahut achchhā khānā banātī hai.
sentences.en: Our daughter-in-law is a wonderful cook.

sentences.native: चाचा जी ताने मारने का एक भी मौक़ा नहीं छोड़ते।
sentences.roman: chāchā jī tāne mārne kā ek bhī mauqā nahīṃ chhoṛte.
sentences.en: Uncle never misses a chance to make a dig.

sentences.native: बड़ों से बात करते समय थोड़ा लिहाज़ रखो।
sentences.roman: baṛoṃ se bāt karte samay thoṛā lihāz rakho.
sentences.en: Show a bit of respect when you talk to elders.

tip.title: बल्कि, चाहे, या तो … या
tip.body:
- **X नहीं, बल्कि Y** = not X but Y · **न सिर्फ़ … बल्कि … भी** = not only … but also.
- **चाहे** + subjunctive = even if / no matter: **चाहे जो हो** 'whatever happens'.
- **या तो … या …** = either … or.
- **… के अलावा** = apart from, besides.
tip.pattern: X नहीं, बल्कि Y  ·  चाहे + subjunctive

sentences.native: गोवा नहीं, बल्कि पहाड़ चलते हैं।
sentences.roman: Govā nahīṃ, balki pahāṛ chalte haiṃ.
sentences.en: Not Goa — let's go to the hills instead.

sentences.native: पहाड़ों में न सिर्फ़ मौसम अच्छा है, बल्कि भीड़ भी कम है।
sentences.roman: pahāṛoṃ meṃ na sirf mausam achchhā hai, balki bhīṛ bhī kam hai.
sentences.en: In the hills not only is the weather nice, there are fewer crowds too.

sentences.native: चाहे जो हो, इस बार हम ज़रूर जाएँगे।
sentences.roman: chāhe jo ho, is bār ham zarūr jāyeṃge.
sentences.en: Whatever happens, we're definitely going this time.

sentences.native: चाहे कितना भी समझाओ, वह नहीं मानेगा।
sentences.roman: chāhe kitnā bhī samjhāo, vah nahīṃ mānegā.
sentences.en: However much you explain, he won't agree.

sentences.native: या तो शुक्रवार को चलो, या फिर अगले हफ़्ते।
sentences.roman: yā to shukravār ko chalo, yā phir agle hafte.
sentences.en: Either we go on Friday, or next week.

sentences.native: मेरे अलावा कोई भी राज़ी नहीं है।
sentences.roman: mere alāvā koī bhī rāzī nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: Nobody's on board apart from me.

sentences.native: अगर तुम मान जाओ, तो बाक़ी सब भी मान जाएँगे।
sentences.roman: agar tum mān jāo, to bāqī sab bhī mān jāyeṃge.
sentences.en: If you come round, everyone else will too.

sentences.native: इसके अलावा, ट्रेन के टिकट भी नहीं मिल रहे।
sentences.roman: iske alāvā, ṭren ke ṭikaṭ bhī nahīṃ mil rahe.
sentences.en: Besides, we can't get train tickets either.

sentences.native: ठीक है, तुम्हारी मर्ज़ी, पर फिर शिकायत मत करना।
sentences.roman: ṭhīk hai, tumhārī marzī, par phir shikāyat mat karnā.
sentences.en: Fine, as you like, but don't complain afterwards.

tip.title: First, then, finally
tip.body:
- Put the plan in order: **सबसे पहले** … **फिर** … **उसके बाद** … **आख़िर में** ….
- Take the floor: **पहले यह बताओ…** · **बात यह है कि…** 'the thing is…'.
- Wrap up: **तो फ़ाइनल रहा?** 'so it's settled?'

sentences.native: सबसे पहले बजट तय करते हैं।
sentences.roman: sabse pahle bajaṭ tay karte haiṃ.
sentences.en: First of all, let's fix the budget.

sentences.native: फिर होमस्टे बुक करेंगे, उसके बाद ट्रेन के टिकट।
sentences.roman: phir homsṭe buk kareṃge, uske bād ṭren ke ṭikaṭ.
sentences.en: Then we'll book the homestay, and after that the train tickets.

sentences.native: आख़िर में देखेंगे कि कौन-कौन आ रहा है।
sentences.roman: āxir meṃ dekheṃge ki kaun-kaun ā rahā hai.
sentences.en: Last of all, we'll see who all is coming.

sentences.native: पहले यह बताओ, सीज़न में होमस्टे कितने का है?
sentences.roman: pahle yah batāo, sīzan meṃ homsṭe kitne kā hai?
sentences.en: First tell me, how much is the homestay in peak season?

sentences.native: बात यह है कि मेरा बजट ज़्यादा नहीं है।
sentences.roman: bāt yah hai ki merā bajaṭ zyādā nahīṃ hai.
sentences.en: The thing is, my budget isn't very big.

sentences.native: दिल्ली से ड्राइव करके जाएँ तो दस घंटे लगेंगे।
sentences.roman: Dillī se ḍrāiv karke jāyeṃ to das ghaṇṭe lageṃge.
sentences.en: If we drive from Delhi it'll take ten hours.

sentences.native: सीज़न से पहले चलें ताकि सब सस्ता मिले।
sentences.roman: sīzan se pahle chaleṃ tāki sab sastā mile.
sentences.en: Let's go before the season so everything's cheaper.

sentences.native: तो फ़ाइनल रहा? शुक्रवार रात को निकलेंगे।
sentences.roman: to fāinal rahā? shukravār rāt ko nikleṃge.
sentences.en: So it's settled? We leave Friday night.

sentences.native: हमने नदी के पास कैंपिंग की, और रात भर गाने गाए।
sentences.roman: hamne nadī ke pās kaimping kī, aur rāt bhar gāne gāye.
sentences.en: We camped by the river and sang songs all night.

sentences.native: पहले दिन बारिश हुई, फिर भी हमने जमकर मज़े किए।
sentences.roman: pahle din bārish huī, phir bhī hamne jamkar maze kiye.
sentences.en: It rained the first day, but we still had a blast.

sentences.native: हम तसल्ली से घूमे, कोई जल्दी नहीं थी।
sentences.roman: ham tasallī se ghūme, koī jaldī nahīṃ thī.
sentences.en: We took our time looking around, there was no rush.

sentences.native: जैसे ही हम पहुँचे, होमस्टे वाली आंटी ने गर्म चाय पिलाई।
sentences.roman: jaise hī ham pahuṃche, homsṭe vālī āṇṭī ne garm chāy pilāī.
sentences.en: As soon as we arrived, the homestay aunty gave us hot tea.

sentences.native: हालाँकि बजट से थोड़ा ज़्यादा ख़र्च हुआ, पर पैसा वसूल था।
sentences.roman: hālāṃki bajaṭ se thoṛā zyādā xarch huā, par paisā vasūl thā.
sentences.en: Although we went a bit over budget, it was totally worth it.

sentences.native: कैंपिंग में जो मज़ा आया, वो किसी होटल में नहीं आता।
sentences.roman: kaimping meṃ jo mazā āyā, vo kisī hoṭal meṃ nahīṃ ātā.
sentences.en: The fun we had camping, you'd never get in a hotel.

sentences.native: अगली बार तुम भी चलना, चाहे जो हो!
sentences.roman: aglī bār tum bhī chalnā, chāhe jo ho!
sentences.en: Next time you're coming too, whatever happens!

sentences.native: अभी तो मैं थका हुआ हूँ, बाक़ी बातें कल तसल्ली से करेंगे।
sentences.roman: abhī to maiṃ thakā huā hūṃ, bāqī bāteṃ kal tasallī se kareṃge.
sentences.en: I'm tired right now, we'll talk about the rest properly tomorrow.
